title: Also there was a large creature puppet that genuinely frightened me w...
transcript: what if there was another Wizard of Oz prequel from the artist behind the beloved Milky White puppet? well good news, there actually was and not only that, there's a pro shot you can watch! and of all the stage productions I've seen it's one of the very few that I would call genuinely flawless welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history if you don't know the puppet designer James Ortiz he's really been making waves in the theatre community recently with puppets that capture our hearts puppets that leave us awestruck and in general just adds so much to every production he works on but the first production where he really garnered widespread attention in the theatre industry was one that he didn't just design the puppets for he also co-conceived, it co-wrote it co-directed it, starred in it, and designed the set it was called The Woodsman and it had multiple major runs in New York from 2013 to 2016 and unlike the Tin Man origin story we get in Wicked The Woodsman takes inspiration from the backstory provided for this character in the original Wizard of Oz novel by L Frank Baum the titular woodsman falls in love with not the Wicked Witch of the east herself but with her assistant so the witch places a curse on his axe, and so on… and the way they achieve his transformation into the Tin Man on stage is so brilliant and beautiful basically what they did was as his limbs get replaced one by one the ensemble would puppeteer the tin limbs moving in conjunction with the live actor. the show used very few spoken words instead relying largely on visual storytelling from both the puppets and live actors which in this show in particular, actually feel like one and the same meanwhile the original live music by Edward W Hardy was just just as significant in telling the story and establishing the overall artistic vision for the production in fact Hardy was the other co-conceiver of the show with James Ortiz really every aspect of it was just beautifully realized to cast a spell on its audience and draw us into the story and the storytelling and not that it's a competition but in its own simpler more tender, intimate way it's just as tragic as Wicked. they also did this cool thing where they left the Tin Man puppet up on stage at the end of the show which was fun as an audience member to like take a closer look at it take a picture of it whatever but it was also justified by the narrative and even added more weight to the ending really giving us this sense that we're leaving him stuck in this spot I guess until Dorothy finds him I really wish this show could come back or would still be running today and I know it's not just me I feel like anytime I talk to someone about this show who's also seen it it's just gushing about how beautiful and special it was but lucky for us there is in fact a professionally filmed video of it which I believe is available on BroadwayHD and if you can I highly recommend watching it
